label: rem:two-photon-pair-production
title: Two photons hitting a heavy nucleus: $\gamma\gamma \to e^- e^+$ as a forced symmetric-crystal step
html:
Remark (concrete example: \gamma\gamma \to e^- e^+ in the symmetric crystal). In the topological ansatz, the photon \gamma is the empty knot \varnothing. This identity element on n strands carries no crossings. It is distinct from the unknot 0_1 representing the neutrino. The two-photon state \gamma\gamma corresponds to the identity element T_e \in H_n(R, q) on n = 2 strands. It has zero crossings, zero graded Hecke energy, and strict bar-invariance. Applying T_e \mapsto \overline{T_e} swaps over- and under-crossings, of which there are none, returning T_e unchanged. The state sits at the highest-weight node of the trivial component of \mathrm{Cryst}^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}).

We place this state at the high-energy boundary of a heavy nucleus. This fixed external boundary condition supplies energy to the crystal traversal. The intense local energy density forces the system to step down the crystal graph to absorb energy. However, symmetric-crystal pair production forbids a unimodal lowering step \gamma\gamma \xrightarrow{\tilde f_i} v landing on a single chiral descendant. The only admissible step is the paired operator:

  \gamma\gamma
  \;\xrightarrow{\;(\tilde f_i,\tilde f_{\bar i})\;}\;
  e^-\,\sqcup\,e^+.

One operator twists two strands into a left-handed trefoil (the electron e^-). The bar-conjugate operator simultaneously twists two strands into the right-handed anti-trefoil (the positron e^+). The bar-conjugate descendant pair conserves the bar-invariance of the source state. Charge (-e + e = 0) and chirality (-\tfrac12 + \tfrac12 = 0) are conserved structurally.

Falsification handle. The symmetric-crystal pair production conjecture forbids any single-photon pair-production channel \gamma \to e^- e^+ without invoking energy–momentum conservation as a separate axiom. The bar-invariant single-strand source state \gamma carries no crossings to fold into a paired operator. Consequently, the symmetric crystal has no admissible step. The empirical absence of \gamma \to e^- e^+ in vacuum is consistent with the conjecture. Observation of this channel without a recoiling external boundary falsifies it.
